title: Work sequence, property protection and public safety
audience: Garden clean-up crews and crew leaders who sequence tasks, set work zones and protect the client's property and the public during a job.
learningOutcomes: Sequence a garden clean-up from secure access and protected surfaces through to collection and transport.
Protect windows, paving, lawns, irrigation fittings and other property from damage during the work.
Set up barriers, exclusion zones and one-way material routes to keep the public and bystanders clear.
Stop work when barriers cannot be maintained and reset the zone before restarting.

instruction.heading: Planning the order of the work
instruction.body: A well-sequenced garden clean-up is safer, faster and less likely to damage the property. Start by confirming access: gates open, paths clear, vehicles able to park, and a safe place to stage tools and waste. Plan the order so that the team works from the cleanest and most secure area toward the messiest, and from the area furthest from the exit toward the gate, so that material is not carried back across finished ground. Clear obstructions such as furniture, pot plants and garden ornaments before cutting. Remove the heaviest or most dangerous items in a controlled way, rather than dragging them across lawns and paving. Plan the route for barrows and trailers before the first load moves. Write the sequence on the job sheet, and brief the team on it before starting.

instruction.heading: Protecting the property
instruction.body: Protect the client's property as carefully as you would protect your own. Cover or move windows, doors and glass that could be struck by a branch, a blower or a thrown clipping. Keep trimmer and mower discharge away from windows, vehicles, and any fragile item. Lay boards or protective matting where a barrow or trailer will cross lawn or soft ground. Do not drive or stand heavy equipment on paving, timber decking, pond edges or raised garden beds unless the surface is known to carry the load. Identify irrigation fittings, valves and sprinkler heads and mark them so that they are not cut or driven over. Report any damage immediately, record it with photographs taken with consent, and tell the client before leaving the site. Never attempt to repair damage to a service or fitting that belongs to a licence holder.

instruction.heading: Public safety and barriers
instruction.body: Garden work is often done close to footpaths, driveways, neighbours and children. Set up exclusion zones around the work area before cutting starts. Use barrier tape, cones or a temporary fence to keep people out, and check that the barrier is still in place at each stage. Where a footpath crosses the site, a spotter should stop pedestrians while material is moved and should watch for vehicles. Do not allow loads to cross public paths unless the route is controlled. Keep material off the footpath and kerb, and keep the stormwater drain clear. If a pedestrian enters the zone, stop the affected work until they have left the zone, and restart only when the barrier is restored. Many people do not realise how far a cutting tool or a flying clipping can travel, so set the zone wider than seems necessary.

instruction.heading: Material movement and stop conditions
instruction.body: Set a one-way material route, so that barrows and bags move from the cutting zone to the collection point without crossing back. Keep the collection point clear of traffic and away from the front entrance. Load barrows and trailers in a balanced way and do not overload them. Secure loose material on trailers before leaving. Stop work and reassess when a barrier cannot be maintained, when a person or animal enters the zone, when material begins to spill onto a footpath, or when a vehicle is manoeuvring nearby. Do not continue because the job is almost complete. Record each stop, the reason and the action taken, and inform the supervisor.

instruction.heading: Verification and escalation
instruction.body: A supervisor should check the layout and the decisions, not only the finished site. A competent worker can point to the work zone, the exclusion zone, the one-way material route, the protected surfaces and the stop conditions, and can explain how they would respond to a pedestrian entering the work zone. Escalate to the supervisor when property damage occurs, when a service or fitting is damaged or exposed, when a barrier cannot be kept in place, and when a member of the public is injured or distressed.

procedure: Confirm access, staging and waste collection points before starting, and note any obstructions.
Write the work sequence on the job sheet, from the most secure area toward the messiest, and brief the team.
Protect windows, doors, decking, paving and irrigation fittings, and mark fittings that must not be cut or driven over.
Set exclusion zones with barriers, cones or a temporary fence, and set a spotter at any footpath crossing.
Set a one-way material route from the cutting zone to the collection point.
Load barrows and trailers in a balanced way and secure loose material before moving it.
Stop work when a barrier fails, a person enters the zone or material spills, and restart only after the zone is restored.
Record damage, stop events and the actions taken, and tell the client before leaving the site.

workedExamples.situation: A footpath crosses the work area. One crew is using cutting tools in the back section while another crew moves wheelbarrows of cuttings along the same route.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you set the zones and the route so that the public and the crews are protected?
workedExamples.reasoning: Set a barrier around the cutting zone wider than the immediate work. Put a spotter at the footpath crossing to stop pedestrians while loads cross. Set a one-way route for the barrows, separate from the cutting crew's path. Do not let the barrows cross the footpath without the spotter. If a pedestrian enters the cutting zone, stop the cutting until they have left and the barrier is restored, and record the stop.

workedExamples.situation: A trimmer throws a clipping that cracks the glass in a side window while the crew is working close to the house.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do first, and what follows?
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop the trimmer and make the area safe. Check whether anyone was hurt and inform the client immediately. Photograph the damage with consent, record it, and do not attempt a repair. Inform the supervisor, and arrange for the client to be told in writing about the damage and the business's process. The protection step should have covered the window before cutting started.

equipmentAndPpe: Barrier tape, cones and a temporary fence or mesh panel
Protective boards and matting for barrows and trailers
Covers and drop sheets for windows, doors and fragile items
Marking stakes or paint for irrigation fittings and service locations
Eye protection, hearing protection and gloves for the planned work

commonErrors.error: Dragging barrows across lawns and paving instead of setting a protected route.
commonErrors.prevention: Lay boards or matting on the route and plan the path before the first load moves.

commonErrors.error: Setting a barrier too close to the cutting zone, so that flying clippings reach the public.
commonErrors.prevention: Set the zone wider than seems necessary and check it at each stage.

commonErrors.error: Letting material roll onto the footpath or into the stormwater drain.
commonErrors.prevention: Cover loads, keep material on site and keep the drain clear.

commonErrors.error: Continuing to cut while a child or pet is near the barrier.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop the affected work at once, and restart only when the zone is clear and the barrier is restored.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The model WHS framework requires the business to manage risks to the public as well as to workers, to the level that is reasonably practicable. Barriers, spotters and exclusion zones are part of that management.
Work near irrigation fittings or services that belong to a licence holder is outside this lesson. Repairs to services, gas lines and electrical fittings must be referred to the licence holder.
Check the council permit and the site traffic plan before closing or using a public footpath.

qualityStandard: The work sequence is written on the job sheet and briefed before work starts.
Protected surfaces and fittings are covered or marked before cutting starts.
Exclusion zones and a one-way route are in place and checked at each stage.
No material has been left on the footpath, kerb or in the drain at the end of the day.
documentationEvidence: Job sheet with the work sequence, access notes and the zone and route plan.
Pre-start check record for barriers, covers and marked fittings.
Damage record with photographs taken with consent, and the client notification.
Stop-event record for any pedestrian entry, barrier failure or spill.
summary: Plan the order of work so the crew moves forward over clean ground and material does not cross back.
Protect windows, paving, decking and irrigation fittings before cutting starts.
Set exclusion zones wider than the cutting zone and use a spotter at any footpath crossing.
Stop when a barrier fails or a person enters the zone, and record the stop.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the best way to move barrows of cuttings across a lawn to the collection point?
options: Drag them straight across the lawn, since the lawn will recover quickly once the cuttings are removed.
Lay boards or matting on a planned one-way route and keep the route away from fragile areas.
Carry the cuttings by hand over the path to save time setting up any boards or matting at all.

knowledgeChecks.question: A pedestrian walks into the cutting zone while a trimmer is running. What should happen?
options: Keep cutting, since the pedestrian will probably walk out quickly and the cutting only takes a few moments more.
Ask the pedestrian to stand still while the work finishes, since the trimmer will be done in just a few seconds.
Stop the affected cutting, let the pedestrian leave the zone, restore the barrier and restart only when the zone is clear.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should material not be left on the footpath or kerb at the end of a job?
options: Because it can create a hazard for the public and can enter the stormwater system.
Because it weighs less when it is wet and the crew wants to move it easily.
Because the council will charge a fee for it the next day and the crew must pay.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say to do with windows, doors and glass that could be struck by a branch, a blower or a thrown clipping?
options: Tape a sign to them only
Ignore them, since the trimmer is quiet
